title: Your Relationship With Your Phone
description: Unpack how you use your devices. Are you the master of your tech, or is your tech the master of you?

questions.pho_1: I feel restless, uncomfortable, and extremely anxious if I realize I've left my phone at home.
questions.pho_2: I often suddenly realize I've just spent an hour scrolling social media feeds with no clear purpose.
questions.pho_3: I consciously turn off most app notifications on my phone (except urgent messages) to protect my focus.
questions.pho_4: I always feel a strong urge to respond to every notification sound as fast as possible.
questions.pho_5: My phone is the first thing I grab and check when I wake up, even before getting out of bed.
questions.pho_6: I often deliberately leave my phone in another room (out of reach) when I need to focus on work or spend time with family.
questions.pho_7: I very often worry about missing important news, the latest gossip, or invitations (FOMO) if I'm not online.
questions.pho_8: Whenever I feel even the slightest boredom (like waiting in an elevator or at a red light), my hand reflexively opens my phone.
questions.pho_9: I regularly and mindfully schedule times (or certain days) for a 'digital detox' (screen-free).
questions.pho_10: If there's a silence of more than a few minutes while I'm texting someone, I start to feel anxious or overthink.
questions.pho_11: I often mean to open my phone just to check the time or one important message, but end up drifting into other apps for ages.
questions.pho_12: I proactively set app time limits (screen time / app limits) and stick to them strictly when the limit is reached.
questions.pho_13: I have a habit of refreshing my email, chats, or feed over and over, hoping for an update or new notification.
questions.pho_14: Scrolling short-video algorithms (like Reels or TikTok) is my easiest way to switch my brain off and escape stressful thoughts.
questions.pho_15: I don't feel guilty at all about replying to messages a bit later because I'm focused on finishing a real-world task.
questions.pho_16: After posting a photo or status on social media, I feel quite stressed thinking about how many likes or comments I'll get.
questions.pho_17: I have a strong habit of double-screening, like scrolling my phone nonstop while a movie is playing on the TV or laptop.
questions.pho_18: Most of my screen time is truly used for very specific, functional purposes (e.g. maps, banking, studying, important communication).
questions.pho_19: Seeing my phone battery below 20% when I'm out makes me very restless and panicked about finding a charger.
questions.pho_20: I very often stay up late past my planned bedtime purely because I get sucked into the algorithm feed.
questions.pho_21: When eating with people close to me, my phone stays in my bag or pocket, not face-up on the table.
questions.pho_22: If my phone isn't in my pocket when my hand reflexively reaches for it, I feel a mini panic attack in my chest.
questions.pho_23: I've repeatedly deleted an entertainment app to limit myself, only to download it again the next day when the craving hits.
questions.pho_24: At the end of the day, I feel I'm the one in full control of my device, not the device dictating my emotions and time.

results.description: You have strong FOMO. You keep checking your phone for fear of missing messages or trends, or of seeming unresponsive.
Your phone is your sacred escape. You scroll endless algorithms for a quick dopamine hit or to flee real-world boredom.
Congratulations! You're very aware of your tech limits. You use your phone as a tool, not as an escape or a source of anxiety.
